key_insight: CURIO augments test-time RL with intrinsic curiosity so an LLM can keep exploring promising but low-reward directions instead of over-committing to early high-reward paths.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to improve adaptive reasoning and discovery systems by balancing exploitation with exploration during inference-time learning.
method: Add an Intrinsic Curiosity World Model (ICWM) that predicts transitions in the policy’s hidden-state space.
Use prediction-error bonuses for sampled tokens outside the policy’s top-k choices to encourage novel exploration.
Normalize bonuses by epoch and anneal their weight when updating the policy.
evidence_signal: Across six math discovery tasks and single-cell denoising with Qwen3 backbones from 8B to 235B, CURIO outperforms a task-only RL control on most objectives, matches the best reported Circle Packing result, and improves denoising metrics at every tested scale.
watch_item: Curiosity bonuses and top-k masking add tuning complexity, so the balance between exploration and task reward may be sensitive to hyperparameters and model scale.
paper_title: CURIO: Curiosity-Driven Test-Time Learning for Open-Ended Discovery
